title: Fate of Existing Overrides at or After the Split Point on a THIS_AND_FUTURE Edit
question: When a THIS_AND_FUTURE edit splits a series at split_rid, what happens to existing single-instance overrides whose RECURRENCE-ID is at or after split_rid?
spec_gap: RFC 5545 states that a RANGE=THISANDFUTURE change does not impact subsequent instances defined in separate components, but a store that splits the series into separate components has no equivalent rule. A THIS_AND_FUTURE delete clearly removes them; for an edit, the overrides may still name valid instances of the new future segment.

citations.verbatim_quote: Subsequent instances are determined by their "RECURRENCE-ID" value and not their current scheduled start time. Subsequent instances defined in separate components are not impacted by the given recurrence instance.

options.summary: Standalone overrides with RECURRENCE-ID >= split_rid are removed; the new future segment starts with no exceptions.
consequences: Simple, and identical to the THIS_AND_FUTURE delete behavior.
Per-instance edits after the split point are silently lost.

options.summary: Standalone overrides with RECURRENCE-ID >= split_rid that are still candidate instances of the new future segment are kept and attached to it (re-keyed to the new UID under NEW_UID, and shifted if the edit shifted the series); the rest are removed.
consequences: Preserves per-instance edits after the split point.
Interacts with this_and_future_split_mode and series_reschedule_exception_mode: re-keying and shifting rules must be defined for each combination.
